script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for October 3. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Oil is concentrated ancient sunlight.  Millions of years of photosynthesis, compressed and stored.  When you burn gasoline, you're releasing solar energy captured before dinosaurs existed.

Fossil fuels are savings—accumulated over eons. Renewables are income—flowing continuously. Living on savings works until they're gone. Transition to income is essential for long-term viability. One gallon of gasoline equals weeks of human labor.  Fossil fuels concentrated enormous energy into convenient packages.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Inherited wealth can be spent quickly.  Know whether you're drawing from income or savings.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Savings vs Income Check - What Are You Depleting?.

Here's your activity: What are your 'fossil fuels'—accumulated resources you're spending? Savings, health, goodwill, reputation built over years? Are you also building new deposits, or just depleting? Balance inheritance spending with income earning. This helps you distinguish stored resources from renewable flows.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about ancient sunlight stored can be applied to savings vs income check - what are you depleting?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
